antagonists.rationale_text: Einstellung-effect undermines input-vs-output-goals by causing practitioners to force new problems into a familiar input framework rather than selecting the right method for the actual output desired.
antagonists.source_quote: Maslow's Hammer describes the cognitive bias where if the only tool you have is a hammer, you treat every problem as if it were a nail, forcing the output to fit the available input method.
antagonists.affinity_rationale: Standard availability/substitution mechanism — persists in using unhelpful frameworks (familiar Inputs) in genuinely novel contexts, forcing Output to fit Input method.
antagonists.activation_condition: When familiar execution frameworks are applied reflexively to genuinely novel goal structures rather than designing input processes from the output backward

antagonists.rationale_text: Curse-of-knowledge undermines input-vs-output-goals by causing experts to communicate complex process details instead of translating their insight into a clear, actionable output message.
antagonists.source_quote: Experts, having dedicated years to mastering the how (complex inputs), often struggle to synthesize and communicate the simple what (clear output/message) to a novice audience. They prioritize the structural edifice over the compelling building blocks.
antagonists.affinity_rationale: Experts prioritize the structural edifice of complex inputs over compelling building blocks — impairs translation of simple output goals to team execution.
antagonists.activation_condition: When experts communicate goal architecture in abstract jargon rather than translating output goals into concrete, actionable input steps for non-expert executors

structured_tensions.tension_text: Input-vs-output-goals conflicts with commitment-bias when teams keep honoring activity commitments even after the result signal has weakened.
structured_tensions.source_quote: input-vs-output-goals conflicts with commitment-bias (commitment bias) when teams keep activity targets despite weak outcome movement.

structured_tensions.tension_text: Input-vs-output-goals conflicts with incentives when reward design makes visible effort easier to optimize than value delivery.
structured_tensions.source_quote: input-vs-output-goals conflicts with incentives (incentives) when reward design over-indexes on visible effort instead of value delivery.
